annotation.title_clean: Person, Thing, Robot: A Moral and Legal Ontology for the 21st Century and Beyond
annotation.title_en: Person, Thing, Robot: A Moral and Legal Ontology for the 21st Century and Beyond
annotation.venue: Frontiers in Artificial Intelligence and Applications, Vol. 397 (Robophilosophy 2024), IOS Press
annotation.summary_en: Conference paper from Robophilosophy 2024 asking what a robot is in moral and legal terms. It rejects both reification and personification of robots and argues for a fundamental reformulation of the person/thing ontology, developing a new approach to technology law and ethics. Only the abstract is available.
key_provisions_or_claims: Robots are things that nonetheless have social presence and invite anthropomorphism.
Fitting robots into existing categories of person or thing is inadequate.
Argues for a revolutionary reformulation of the moral and legal ontology.
Proposes a new approach to technology law and ethics that can scale to future challenges.
